title: Forever, if you want it
text: For years you've noticed the same pale figure at the edge of every streetlight. Tonight they finally speak: "I can give you forever. All it costs is the sun."

outcomes.text: A sharp kiss at the throat, then nothing. I woke up hungry, and the world had never looked so sharp.
They took too much. I came back three nights later in a drawer with a tag on my toe, and I have never forgiven them for the waiting.
I ran until my lungs burned. When I looked back, the street was empty.
I ran. They were already waiting at my door. They don't take no for an answer.
I drove a broken chair leg into its chest. It crumbled into ash. Nobody will ever believe me.
It laughed as I swung. Then it bit me.

title: The candles light themselves
text: Every candle in your bedroom flickers alight when you walk in. The curtains stir. Your mother is standing in the doorway, and she doesn't look surprised.

outcomes.text: "It skips a generation, usually," she said, and pulled an old book from under the stairs. My lessons started that night.
She went very still and told me to never say that word in her house again. She had spent her whole life not being what I am.
I taught myself from library books and trial and error. The neighbor's cat now follows me everywhere.
I taught myself badly. Something came through the practice circle that I could not put back, and it took two years to undo.
I blew the candles out and refused to think about it. Sometimes, when I'm angry, the lights still flicker.
I pushed it down for twenty years, and it came back up all at once in the middle of an argument in a supermarket.

title: Something is different
text: In the middle of gym class, you catch a ball that was going to hit someone's head. Only you caught it from across the room. Everyone saw something. Nobody is sure what.

outcomes.text: I started sneaking out at night. The city has a new rumor, and it's me.
My first save went badly. I got the child out and put a car through a shopfront doing it.
Why should I be the one who plays fair? I started planning.
I used it for myself exactly once, got away with it easily, and never seriously considered another way again.
I kept it quiet and blamed it on adrenaline. But I practice when nobody's looking.
I hid it so well that I half convinced myself. It took a car on top of somebody's legs to bring it back.

title: The alley
text: A shortcut home. A figure in the alley. Cold fingers on your neck before you can scream.

outcomes.text: I woke up in the gutter at dawn with two small holes in my neck and a hunger no food could touch.
I broke free and ran. The doctor said the bite was from a dog. It wasn't.
It fed, and then, for reasons I'll never know, it gave me a drink of its own blood. I've been different ever since.
It fed and left me there. I spent a week in hospital with no memory of that night.
I said please. They stopped, looked at me properly for the first time, and left me on the ground alive.
I begged, and being begged at turned out to be the part they had been waiting for.

title: The spill
text: A containment tank ruptures at the research park next to you. Green light. A roar. Then silence.

choices.label: Pull people out of the building

outcomes.text: I carried four people out. The next morning I lifted my car with one hand.
I pulled two people out before the smoke got me. I woke up in hospital with nothing but a cough.
I ran and never looked back. The rash went away after a month.
I got away clean, or so I thought. Weeks later, the lights started bending toward me. I decided to cash in.
I went towards it instead of away. Whatever was in that tank is in me now.
I went back for a sample and got a lungful of it and eleven months in a hospital bed.

title: Grandmother's book
text: Clearing out a relative's attic, you find a heavy leather book. Your name is written inside the cover, in handwriting older than you are.

outcomes.text: The words tasted like thunder. By the last page, I could make water boil by looking at it.
Nothing happened. Then all the mirrors in the house cracked at once. I burned the book.
A very polite woman paid me cash and asked me never to look for her.
The collector paid well and came back a year later wanting to know what else was in that attic. He was not polite the second time.
Some doors should stay closed.
I put it back, and it was on my kitchen table in the morning. I put it back twice more before I stopped trying.

title: A royal at the bar
text: The quiet person you've been chatting with all night asks if you'd like to visit the palace. They're serious. They're {r.first}, and they're royalty.

outcomes.text: One visit became many. A year later, I married into the royal family, and my face was on every magazine cover.
The family found out who I was and made sure I never saw {r.first} again.
I let it go. Sometimes I see {r.first} on the news and wonder.
I said no, and {r.first} kept writing for eleven years. The last letter came from a different palace.

choices.label: Go, but keep your own life

outcomes.text: I kept my flat, my job and my friends, and visited the palace at weekends. It lasted longer than anybody predicted.
I tried to keep both and the palace made it quietly impossible. I chose, in the end, the way they knew I would.

title: The hunters
text: Crosses nailed to your door. A photograph of you, from 1970-something, slid under it. They know what you are.

outcomes.text: I left everything and started over under a new name.
I ran, and they had somebody waiting at the port. I got out of the country with a stake wound and no luggage.

choices.label: Wait for them in the dark

outcomes.text: There were three of them. There are none now.
They were ready for me. I escaped with a stake wound an inch from my heart.
Their leader was dying. I offered him forever. Now the hunters work for me.
They weren't interested in talking.

title: Unmasked
text: A photo is all over the internet: you, mid-transformation, half in costume. Reporters are camped outside your home.

outcomes.text: I took off the mask in front of every camera in the city. My life will never be private again.
I owned it, and within a month my family had moved twice and my old employer was being doorstepped.
I blamed it on a lookalike and a good editor. Half the internet believes me.
Nobody believed me. Now I'm a liar and a freak.
I moved away and changed my name. I miss my old life.
I disappeared so completely that the city decided I had died, and put up a plaque.

title: Witch hunt
text: Someone saw. A church group has your photo on a flyer, and a crowd is gathering on your lawn with phones, signs and at least one pitchfork.

outcomes.text: I talked. They listened, mostly. A few of them came back later to ask for help.
Someone threw a rock. Then everyone did.
Every phone in the crowd died at once. So did the streetlights. They ran, and they're too scared to come back.
I threw everything I had at them and it worked and it was filmed from four windows.
I packed my herbs and my cat and left before dawn.
I left, and they burned the house anyway. Everything I had inherited went with it.

title: Revolution
text: The palace gates are chained from the outside. Tens of thousands are in the square chanting your name, and not kindly.

outcomes.text: I left in the night with what jewels I could carry. The monarchy ended with me.
outcomes.milestone: was overthrown and fled into exile

outcomes.text: I abdicated at dawn and walked out of the front gate on foot, and the square let me through.
outcomes.milestone: abdicated and walked out through the crowd

outcomes.text: The square was cleared by morning. History will not be kind to me.
The soldiers refused. They opened the gates instead.
outcomes.milestone: was overthrown by their own army

outcomes.text: I signed away most of my powers on live television. The crowd went quiet, then cheered.
I offered a constitution and they read it as weakness. The chanting started again before the ink was dry.

title: Front page
text: A tabloid has a long-lens photo of you, looking very undignified on a friend's yacht.

outcomes.text: The courts sided with me. The paper printed a tiny apology.
The trial kept the photo in the news for months.
My joke about it went viral. People like me more now.
The palace was not amused.
It blew over. Eventually.
I said nothing, and the silence let them run it for nine days with a new photograph each morning.

title: A state visit
text: A foreign head of state is visiting, and protocol says you host the banquet.

outcomes.text: By dessert we were swapping stories. The trade deal went through the next week.
My joke about their country did not translate.
Dignified, correct, and forgotten by morning.
I kept it strictly to protocol and their delegation took the coolness personally. The trade talks stalled for a year.

choices.label: Put something of your own in the programme

outcomes.text: I dropped the state orchestra for a choir from the town I grew up in. It was the only part of the evening anybody reported.
The palace staff were appalled and the visiting delegation more so. Protocol exists for reasons I had to be told about afterwards.

title: An heir, unannounced
text: A young woman comes forward claiming her child is a royal heir. Yours, specifically.

outcomes.text: It's not mine. The story died overnight.
It's mine. The line of succession just got longer.
Money made it go away. For now.
I paid, and the payment itself became the story eight years later. The child was not the scandal; the cheque was.
I stood on the steps and said the child's name. Half the country thought better of me for it.
I acknowledged {k.first}, and the succession lawyers have been arguing about it ever since.

title: Jubilee
text: The nation wants a jubilee to celebrate your family.

choices.label: Throw the biggest party in a century

outcomes.text: Street parties in every town. The nation loved it.
Critics called it a waste of money during hard times.
A quiet service and a tree planting. Tasteful.
I kept it modest during a hard year and the country noticed, in the way countries do, all at once and warmly.

choices.label: Spend the budget on the country instead

outcomes.text: No parade. Two hundred new beds in three hospitals with the family name nowhere on them.
I gave the jubilee money away and the papers ran a fortnight of stories about a monarchy too embarrassed to celebrate itself.

title: Abolish the monarchy?
text: A popular politician has tabled a bill to abolish the monarchy.

outcomes.text: I toured the country. The bill failed by a wide margin.
Royals aren't supposed to do politics. It backfired.
The bill failed without my help. Barely.
I stayed out of it and the bill passed its second reading. Staying above politics turned out to be a position too.
We talked for three hours. He still wants to abolish me, but he withdrew the bill and said why.
He came, ate, and used every detail of the afternoon in a book that sold extremely well.

title: A cousin's ambition
text: Your cousin {c.first} has been quietly telling courtiers that the crown would suit them better.

outcomes.text: {c.first} backed down, but the smile never reached their eyes.
{c.first} laughed and denied everything.
A few dinners and a lot of flattery later, the whispers stopped.
I bought the room back and {c.first} bought it again the following season. It has been going on for years.
I handed {c.first} a genuine portfolio and a genuine amount of work. The whispers stopped because {c.he} no longer had time.
I gave {c.first} real power and {c.he} used it exactly as {c.he} had always said {c.he} would.

title: An old face
text: At a gallery opening you see {x.first}, someone you loved decades ago, now grey and stooped. They recognize you instantly.

outcomes.text: We talked until closing. They cried. I couldn't.
They screamed that I was a ghost. The security guards remember my face now.
I left before they could reach me. Some things are kinder unsaid.
I walked away and heard afterwards that {x.first} had told everyone at the opening about a face that had not aged in forty years.
I told {x.first} everything, in a gallery corridor, at eighty-one years old. {x.He} believed me immediately, which was the part I had not prepared for.
I told {x.first} the truth and {x.he} told the room, and the room told a journalist who does this sort of story.

title: The blood bank
text: A night-shift orderly at the hospital blood bank has figured out what you are. He's offering a deal.

outcomes.text: Two bags a month, no questions asked. The thirst is manageable now.
He sold me out to the hunters instead.
Nobody will miss a night-shift orderly. That's what I told myself.
He had left a letter with a friend, to be opened if anything happened to him. The police read it out to me.
I don't trust anyone who trades in blood.
I refused, and he took it as a threat and went to a journalist with what he thought he knew.

title: Caught out
text: You lost track of time. The sky is turning grey and you are twenty minutes from home.

outcomes.text: I made it with seconds to spare, smoking at the edges.
I didn't make it in time. The burns will take years to fade.
I spent the day in a stranger's cellar. They never knew.
The homeowner came down for the laundry.
I knocked, said I was in trouble, and a woman in a dressing gown let me into her cellar without asking a single question.
I knocked, and they opened the curtains to see who it was.

title: No reflection
text: A friend is scrolling through photos from a party. You aren't in any of them, though you were standing right there.

outcomes.text: "I'm just very photogenic," I said. They laughed. Mostly.
The joke landed and then somebody scrolled back through three years of photographs and stopped laughing.
One look and they forgot the whole party.
I took the evening out of them and something else came away with it. They have never been quite the same person since.

choices.label: Tell them what they are looking at

outcomes.text: I said it plainly, expecting the worst. They decided it was the best thing that had ever happened to them.
I told them, and watched somebody I liked work out over about four seconds that they were alone in a room with me.

title: A reckless fledgling
text: One of the people you turned is feeding openly. The news is calling it 'the Night Slasher'.

outcomes.text: I found them before the police did. They listen to me now.
I found them and they laughed at me. I made them stop, and that is the last conversation we ever had.
I made the choice I should have made the day I turned them.
I ended them, and found out afterwards the killings had never been theirs at all.
I made the killings mine, publicly, and moved cities. They got to keep a life I had already ruined once.
I took the blame and they carried on doing it anyway, now with somebody else's name on it.

title: A cure?
text: A disgraced hematologist claims to have reversed vampirism in a rat. She wants a volunteer.

outcomes.text: Three weeks of agony. Then my heart started beating again. I'm mortal, and I'm aging.
The treatment didn't work. It nearly killed me, which is a hard thing to do.
Forever is mine. No one gets to take it away.
I burned the research, and the woman who wrote it spent the rest of her life trying to reconstruct it out of spite.
I paid for the lab, the rats and eleven years. She got there in the end and I was the first human trial.
outcomes.milestone: funded the cure for their own condition

outcomes.text: I funded her for eleven years and she died two months before the trial. Nobody else could read her notes.

title: Your own funeral
text: Your family went ahead with your funeral. You can hear it from behind the cemetery wall.

outcomes.text: They said kind things. More than I deserved.
I listened to the whole service from behind the wall, and learned two things about myself I would rather not have.
Screaming. Fainting. My aunt had to be sedated.
I walked in, and my mother simply held onto me and would not let go. Nobody else could look at either of us.
I put three words on the windscreen of my brother's car and walked away before the service ended.
I left a note, and it was read out at the wake as evidence that somebody was playing a very cruel joke.

title: The smell
text: People are wrinkling their noses when you pass. The cologne isn't helping any more.

outcomes.text: Formaldehyde and a steady hand. I'll last a while longer.
I did it myself and did it badly. The smell went; so did most of the feeling in my left side.
People keep moving seats on the bus.
I ignored it until a colleague reported a gas leak and the building was evacuated twice.

choices.label: Find someone who does this professionally

outcomes.text: A mortician three towns over asked no questions and did excellent work. We have an arrangement now.
The mortician did the work and then worked out what he had been working on.

title: A medium
text: A medium at a carnival grabs your wrist, goes white, and whispers: 'You shouldn't be here.'

outcomes.text: "Finish what you came back for," she said, and refused my money.
She told me what I had come back for. I had been hoping it was something better than that.
I haven't slept since. Not that I need to.
I walked off, and she followed me three streets to press a folded paper into my hand. I have never opened it.

choices.label: Ask her who sent you back

outcomes.text: She gave me a name. I recognised it, which was the worst possible answer.
She would not say it out loud. She wrote it down, burned the paper, and refused to look at me again.

title: Building fire
text: An apartment block is burning. The fire crews are twenty minutes out. People are screaming at the windows.

outcomes.text: I got every family out. A photo of my silhouette in the flames made the front page.
I saved most of them. Not all. I keep seeing the one I couldn't reach.
They did their best. The news said three people died.
I stayed on the pavement and a firefighter died going in. I have run the arithmetic on that a thousand times.

choices.label: Go in with your face covered

outcomes.text: Nobody got a clear look at me. Eleven people came out of that building and none of them can say who carried them.
The mask slipped on the fourth floor in front of a man who has been looking for me ever since.

title: An offer
text: A masked figure leaves a card at your door: "Your talents are wasted. Join us. Name your price."

outcomes.text: I learned their plans and brought the whole crew down.
They spotted the wire. I barely got out.
The money is very good. My conscience is quieter than I expected.
I took the offer and found out within a year that I had joined something with a hierarchy, and that I was near the bottom of it.
I have enough enemies.
I burned it, and a second card arrived every year for a decade, each one more accurate about my life than the last.

title: The vault
text: Your crew has found a bank moving gold through the city tonight. They want you on the job.

outcomes.text: We took the whole shipment. The city is terrified of us now.
A hero was waiting. I got away. My crew didn't.
The crew went without me. They got caught, and they're talking.
The crew went without me and came back rich, and made very sure I knew exactly what my caution had cost me.
I made one call from a phone box. The crew went down and never worked out where it came from.
I tipped them off, and one of the crew was arrested holding a list with my name on it.

title: Growing stronger
text: Your powers are changing. Stronger, and harder to control.

outcomes.text: I'm faster, stronger, sharper. I barely recognize myself.
I trained until something in it slipped, and spent a fortnight unable to touch anything without breaking it.
I'm scared of what I might become.
Holding back did not keep it still. It came out on its own at the worst possible moment.

choices.label: Find somebody who has been through it

outcomes.text: There was somebody older, quieter and further along than me, and a fortnight with them did more than a year of guessing.
The only person I found who had been through it had come out the other side as something I did not want to be.

title: Key to the city
text: The mayor wants to give your alter ego the key to the city at a public ceremony.

outcomes.text: The crowd went wild. Kids were dressed as me.
Someone in the third row took a very good photograph of my jaw, and it has been circulating ever since.
Mysterious. The press loved that even more.
The mayor took the note as an insult and spent the rest of his term explaining that the city did not need me.

choices.label: Send a kid from the neighbourhood instead

outcomes.text: I sent a fourteen-year-old who had pulled two people out of a canal that spring. The photograph of her holding it is still on that wall.
The mayor's office took it as a stunt and the story became about me refusing to appear.

title: A knock at night
text: Your neighbor {n.first} is on your doorstep, crying. Their child is sick and the doctors don't know why. They've heard rumors about you.

outcomes.text: I sat with the child all night. By morning the fever broke. {n.first} tells everyone I'm a saint.
I tried everything I knew. It wasn't enough.
I gave them the name of a good doctor and closed the door.
I sent them to a specialist, who found it in time. {n.first} never knew how close I came to doing something stupider.

choices.label: Help, and tell them exactly what you are

outcomes.text: I told {n.first} what I was doing while I did it. The child recovered and {n.first} has never once mentioned it to anyone.
I told {n.first} the truth, and the child got better, and within a year there was a queue at my door every evening.

title: Blood moon
text: A blood moon tonight. Every witch knows what that means: power, for anyone brave enough to take it.

outcomes.text: Magic poured into me like wine. I've never felt so strong.
Something answered that wasn't meant to. I lost a week of memories.
I drew the curtains and made tea.
I stayed in, and by morning every other witch in the county had more power than me and knew it.
Seven of us in a field, and what we raised together none of us could have raised alone.
We raised it together and then spent a year arguing about whose it had been.

title: Rival coven
text: A rival coven has been hexing your clients. Business is suffering and your cat won't come inside.

outcomes.text: It was over in a flash of green. They left town by morning.
I lost. My hair has been silver ever since.
Tea, cake and a treaty signed in ink and blood. We're allies now.
They signed the treaty and kept hexing the clients quietly enough that it took me two years to prove it.

choices.label: Find out who is paying them

outcomes.text: Somebody was. A competitor of mine, entirely non-magical, with a chequebook and a grudge.
Nobody was paying them. They simply disliked me, which was somehow much harder to deal with.

title: Psychic hotline
text: A late-night TV channel wants you to host a live psychic phone-in show. Real magic would make great television.

outcomes.text: My readings were uncanny. Ratings soared. So did the attention.
I read a caller too accurately on live television and the clip has been analysed frame by frame ever since.
Cold reading and a good voice. Easy money.
I faked it for a year and then a caller described her own kitchen to me before I could, and I could not fake my way out of that.
Magic isn't a party trick.
I turned it down, and they hired somebody with no gift at all who made a fortune pretending to have mine.

title: The cat spoke
text: Your familiar looked you in the eye tonight and said, quite clearly, 'We need to talk about the basement.'

outcomes.text: There was a door there I'd never seen before. Behind it, a library.
There was a door, and behind it something that had been waiting long enough to be extremely patient about it.
The cat has been sulking for a month.
I pretended not to hear, and the cat did not speak again for eleven years. When it did, it was too late for the basement.

choices.label: Ask the cat how long it has been able to talk

outcomes.text: "Since your grandmother," it said, and then told me what she had kept down there and why.
It thought about it for a long moment and then said it could not remember not being able to, which I have decided not to think about.

title: Rationing
text: The war has reached the pumps. Fuel is rationed and prices have tripled.

outcomes.text: I sold the car and bought a bicycle. My legs have never been stronger.
I sold the car for almost nothing in the first week, and the ration was lifted in the second.
It's eating my savings, but I'm not giving up the car.
I paid whatever it cost for four years, and by the end I was queuing at four in the morning for the privilege.

choices.label: Buy fuel on the black market

outcomes.text: Cheaper, no questions asked. Mostly.
It was watered down and wrecked my engine.

title: Refugees
text: Families fleeing the war are arriving in your town with nothing. The shelter is asking for volunteers and spare rooms.

outcomes.text: The {f.last} family lived with me for a year. We still have dinner every Sunday.
They stayed eight months and it was harder than anybody admits out loud. We parted politely and have not spoken since.
I sorted donations every weekend. It helped more than I expected.
I volunteered for a month and stopped going. I have never worked out how to talk about why.
It's not my problem, I told myself.
I kept out of it, and the family who moved in next door turned out to be the ones I had decided not to think about.

title: Lockdown
text: The pandemic has shut the city. Schools, offices, bars, all closed for months.

outcomes.text: I learned to bake, to code and to cut my own hair. Two of those went well.
I started four things and finished none of them, and then felt worse about that than about the lockdown.

choices.label: Break the rules for a party

outcomes.text: It was the best night of the year. Then half the guests got sick.
The police broke it up. The fine was eye-watering.

choices.label: Stay home and wait it out

outcomes.text: Months of the same four walls. I'm not the same person I was.
I stayed in, and the quiet turned out to suit me. I have not been as busy since, on purpose.

title: Panic buying
text: Supermarket shelves are empty. People are fighting over toilet paper.

outcomes.text: My garage looks like a warehouse. I feel prepared and slightly ashamed.
I stocked up, and then spent the rest of the year quietly leaving things on other people's doorsteps to get rid of the feeling.
I did the shopping for the whole street. They left cakes on my doorstep for months.
I shopped for everyone and caught it doing it. Six weeks of being the one the street left cakes for.
I bought my normal shop and went home. It felt like a small act of not joining in, which is most of what I managed that year.
I refused to stockpile and then spent three weeks eating whatever was left at the back of the shelves at nine on a Tuesday night.

title: Replaced by software
text: Your employer has announced that an AI system will handle much of your department's work.

outcomes.text: I became the person who knows how to use the new system. My job is safer than ever.
I tried. They replaced me anyway.
We won a two-year delay. Management will remember my name.
We organised, and management restructured the department around the four of us who had signed the letter.
I left before the axe fell.
I jumped early into a job that was automated eighteen months later, which was at least a shorter wait the second time.

title: A coin to the moon
text: Everyone at work is talking about a new cryptocurrency that has gone up 4,000% this month.

outcomes.text: It went up another 900%. I sold at the top, somehow.
The founders vanished with everyone's money.
I watched from the sidelines, feeling either smart or stupid depending on the day.
I stayed out, and every colleague who did not lost everything within the year. Nobody at work mentions it now.

choices.label: Put in what you can afford to lose

outcomes.text: I put in two weeks' pay, watched it go up eleven times, and took the original stake back out and left the rest to ride.
I put in what I could afford to lose and lost it, which is the only honest outcome of a sentence like that.

title: Bidding war
text: The housing bubble is in full swing. Houses on your street are selling in a day for way over asking.

choices.label: Jump in before it's too late

outcomes.text: I bought at the top of the market. Fingers crossed.
I got outbid eleven times and won the twelfth by paying an amount I still do not say out loud.
Prices kept climbing, and I kept waiting.
I waited, and eighteen months later the street was full of for-sale signs nobody was answering.

choices.label: Buy somewhere nobody is bidding on

outcomes.text: I bought two suburbs out and a bus ride from everything. Ten years later it was the street everyone wanted.
I bought where it was cheap, and found out why it was cheap over the following four winters.

title: Climate strike
text: Millions are marching for climate action. Your friends are going and they want you there.

outcomes.text: We shut down the city center. It felt like history.
I got arrested for blocking a road. The fine stung.
I watched it on the news.
I stayed home, and my friends came back lit up about it and I did not know what to say to any of them.
I brought water, a first aid kit and a folding chair for anybody who needed to sit down. I was the most popular person on that march.
I went prepared and the day turned. I spent the evening in a holding cell with a first aid kit I had not been allowed to keep.

title: A ticket to orbit
text: The space race is on, and a new company is running a lottery: one member of the public goes to orbit.

outcomes.text: I won. I've seen the whole planet in one window.
outcomes.milestone: went to space as a lottery winner

outcomes.text: I didn't win. Of course I didn't.

choices.label: Enter your name for somebody else

outcomes.text: I entered in my daughter's name. She did not win, and she has never stopped talking about the fact that I tried.
I entered for my brother, and he won, and watching the launch from the ground was the strangest afternoon of my life.
Nine minutes of weightlessness for the rest of my life spent being the person who went to space. I passed.
I did not enter, and the winner came from my own street, and I have had to be pleased about it at three separate parties.

title: Election season
text: The election is tight and the campaign in your district is desperate for volunteers.

outcomes.text: Our candidate won by 212 votes. I'll take some of the credit.
We lost. Badly.
I changed nobody's mind and lost two friends.
I argued online for six weeks and something I wrote at two in the morning was screenshotted and passed around my workplace.
I counted ballots until four in the morning. Nobody argued with me once and I have believed in the result ever since.
I worked the count and saw enough small sloppiness to lose a bit of faith in something I would rather have kept.

title: A breakthrough trial
text: A clinical trial for a new longevity treatment is looking for volunteers your age.

outcomes.text: I feel ten years younger. My blood work agrees.
The side effects were brutal.

choices.label: Wait for the results of somebody else's trial

outcomes.text: I let other people go first and joined the third cohort, by which point they knew the dose.
I waited, and the trial was stopped after the second cohort for reasons they did not publish.
I have had enough of doctors. I would rather have the years I have than borrow some.
I stayed out, and watched two people my age who did not get a decade I was not offered again.

title: Called to testify
text: A government committee wants you to testify about how much tax your companies actually pay.

outcomes.text: The clips of me admitting it went everywhere. So did the new tax law.
I told the truth and the committee decided the truth was worth investigating properly.
I said 'I don't recall' forty-one times. It was a meme for a month.
I stonewalled, and one of my own executives went back the following week and did not.
They were very expensive and very effective.
My lawyers were magnificent, and the footage of eleven of them arriving in convoy did more damage than anything I could have said.

title: A kidnapping plot
text: Your security team has intercepted plans to kidnap you on your way to a charity gala.

outcomes.text: I travel with twelve guards now. I haven't walked down a street alone in years.
I doubled the security and one of the new hires turned out to be the reason the plot existed.
The police caught the whole crew in the act. I was a hero for a week.
It went wrong. I spent three terrifying days in a basement before they took the ransom.

choices.label: Find out who is behind it

outcomes.text: It was somebody I had put out of business in 1994. I paid off his debts anonymously and never heard another word.
It was a relative. I have never told the rest of the family and I never will.

title: The heirs are circling
text: Your children are fighting in the press over who will run the empire when you're gone.

outcomes.text: One child is thrilled. The others aren't speaking to me.
I named a successor, and the one I named turned out not to want it at all.
Peace, for now. The lawyers are already sharpening their pencils.
I split it equally and they spent the next decade buying each other out, badly.
They're furious. The world is impressed.
I left it to charity, and two of my children never spoke to me again. The foundation is doing good work.

title: The bunker
text: Your billionaire friends are all building doomsday bunkers in New Zealand. They say you're naive not to.

outcomes.text: Twelve floors underground, a hydroponic farm, and a cinema. I hope I never use it.
I built it, and the contractor sold the plans and the coordinates to somebody else entirely.
If the world ends, I'd rather be above ground.
I laughed at them publicly, and the quote followed me through every crisis for the rest of my life.
I put the bunker money into water treatment for a region that needed it. If the world ends I will take my chances with everyone else.
outcomes.milestone: spent a fortune on something other than themselves

outcomes.text: I built it, put my name on nothing, and read for ten years about how billionaires never do anything for anyone.

title: Tornado warning
text: The sirens are wailing and the sky has turned green.

outcomes.text: It passed two streets over. We came up to find the neighbor's trampoline in our yard.
It came straight down our street. We came up into daylight where the stairs used to have a house on top of them.
Eleven of us and two dogs in a basement built for four. It was the best night that street ever had.
I spent the warning going door to door instead of getting down the stairs, and made it back with about nine seconds to spare.

choices.label: Stand on the porch and watch it

outcomes.text: I watched the whole thing cross two fields. It is the most frightening and the most beautiful thing I have ever seen.
I watched a bit too long. The porch roof went first and took most of my left arm's opinion about things with it.

title: The big city
text: Your rent went up again. Your landlord says there's a line of people who'd pay more.

outcomes.text: I'm working to pay rent now. That's the deal in this city.
I paid it, and he put it up again the following year, and I understood that this was simply the arrangement now.
{r.first} is tidy, quiet and never home. I won the lottery.

choices.label: Move out to where the rent makes sense

outcomes.text: Two hours of commuting a day bought me a flat with a door that closes properly and money left at the end of the month.
I moved out and lost the city entirely: the friends, the evenings, the reason I had come. The rent was lovely.
